archive_06_001.speaker: narrator
archive_06_001.text: The winter kitchen opened its sealed stores on the thirty-seventh morning. The cook weighed the first components into her normal pots and entered ten daily shares against the resident roster. Tan marked half a charcoal sack for the mild day's occupied hall. Neither movement looked momentous. The store sheet now had an opening quantity, a real issue and a remaining balance. Yue ate breakfast beside the same chipped bowl she had used in autumn, aware that the new appointment changed her dates more visibly than her morning.

archive_06_002.speaker: narrator
archive_06_002.text: He arrived carrying a parcel from his father, who would reach the lower receiving house later that day. The parcel contained repaired winter gloves for He's mother and a small packet of money. He had been asked to deliver both, though he could have refused the private task. He set the parcel on his own knees while waiting for the case clerk. The gloves were made from two kinds of leather, stiff where the repaired seams crossed. He turned them over slowly as if looking for a sentence hidden under the stitches.

archive_06_003.speaker: narrator
archive_06_003.text: The registrar's completion bundle had finally supplied a clear result about the later revision. The proposed house revocation had not been registered. The endorsement referred the founder to a separate tenancy procedure, and the office recorded no completed replacement instrument before his death. That established the recovered descendant clause's legal existence. It did not settle whether the family had fulfilled its maintenance condition, whether the trustees owed remedies for their later occupation decisions, or how the current occupant could lawfully remain. The preliminary session would identify those questions with all parties notified.

archive_06_004.speaker: narrator
archive_06_004.text: He read the registry extract three times. His mother's earlier request had been answered as if the descendant clause did not exist, and that answer was now contradicted by a completed official trail. The clerk helped him distinguish that finding from immediate possession. He did not ask for a key this time. He asked for an exact copy of the record saying the revocation was uncompleted. Yue prepared the permitted certified extract under Dai's check, and the clerk gave him its issue receipt. The sheet would survive a conversation that no one could keep perfectly.

archive_06_005.speaker: narrator
archive_06_005.text: The session was set for the forty-fourth day at the lower receiving house. The house occupant could attend through his appointed contact if his health or the road prevented travel. The retired boundary clerk's statement would enter under the ordinary procedure, with further questions reserved if needed. Witnesses still in the district received the same date through the registrar. The archive had supplied its sources and procedural account; it would host neither judge nor verdict in its own workroom. Luo disliked losing the central table, then said aloud that this was probably useful.

archive_06_006.speaker: narrator
archive_06_006.text: Yue's assignment for the session would be source support: identify the archive extracts, answer handling questions within her actual knowledge and bring the required certified movement record. The registrar's own scribe would keep the formal hearing notes. Dai would answer for the catalogue and authorisation failures. He would speak as a claimant, not as the archive's courier. The different roles reduced the room's chance of mistaking a helpful young worker for someone who had investigated his own family beyond criticism. He accepted the distinction with more composure than he had managed on the ridge.

archive_06_007.speaker: narrator
archive_06_007.text: He's father came to the mountain on the thirty-eighth afternoon. He walked the last ascent slowly with a wrapped right hand held close to his chest. The injury was old, and cold made it stiff. He carried no impressive employer's token. A bag of patched clothes hung over his sound shoulder, and his boots had been mended where the toes bent. He waited outside the archive because his son had asked to meet there before returning to the rented rooms. Yue saw He come through the gate and stop before either spoke.

archive_06_008.speaker: narrator
archive_06_008.text: The father reached for the carrying strap as he might once have done when He was smaller. He stepped back and said he had already delivered the parcel. The father lowered his hand. They stood on opposite sides of the yard drain until the cook came out with a broom and asked them to move away from the wet edge. The interruption gave both somewhere else to stand. He pointed toward the bench. His father sat carefully, and the son remained standing for another moment before taking the far end.

archive_06_009.speaker: narrator
archive_06_009.text: Yue had work in the adjoining room and did not remain at the window. Later He told her they had begun by discussing the bridge, because it was a subject on which neither could immediately injure the other. The father knew a different river crossing from his work district. He knew how quickly a worker could lose a week's pay when a route closed. He knew almost nothing of his son's courier rates now. He asked, and He answered. The conversation was small enough that they could continue it.

archive_06_010.speaker: narrator
archive_06_010.text: The father's offered statement covered the years before departure. He had helped with the path drain, bought tools for one repair and later left after the hand injury made local lifting work impossible. He could identify his own actions but not certify every task his wife performed afterwards. The registrar would receive those limited fields if he signed them. His private employment disappointments were not required to prove a school drain had been cleared. He seemed surprised to learn that the hearing did not need him to expose every year he had failed to explain.

archive_06_011.speaker: he_xi
archive_06_011.text: When he began naming his wages, I wanted him to keep talking until the years became a number I could understand. Then I thought of the survey clerk refusing to remember words he had not heard. My father's low wages do not erase what he left my mother to do. They may explain why he sent so little. I can ask him those questions as his son. I do not have to make the registrar hold them all merely because a hearing gives us a table.

archive_06_012.speaker: narrator
archive_06_012.text: His mother arrived after her paid kitchen shift in the village. She accepted the repaired gloves and tried them on without making the gift answer for the rest. The father's hand shook while she flexed the leather fingers. She asked whether the seams would loosen with warmth. He said they would. For several seconds they looked like an ordinary couple discussing a useful repair. Then she asked why he had not written after the previous winter, and the ordinary room widened around a silence their son could not mend.

archive_06_013.speaker: narrator
archive_06_013.text: The family went home together before the evening public hour. Dai let the case desk close on schedule. Their conversation belonged outside it, and a clerk's eagerness to preserve developments would have made the archive an audience rather than a service. Yue completed two standard extracts for other readers while the new stove warmth drifted along the hall. One reader wanted a pasture boundary; another wanted the school endowment's maintenance clause. The ordinary requests helped her remember that the institution served more than the people whose stories she now knew.

archive_06_014.speaker: narrator
archive_06_014.text: In the rented rooms, the father found the little table he had made before leaving. One leg had been repaired twice in his absence, first badly, then with a neat brace. He touched the brace and asked who had fitted it. His wife said the neighbour did it after she grew tired of spilled soup. He thanked the neighbour's absent name as if speaking to the wood. He Xi wanted to tell him there were many such repairs. Instead he helped carry the table closer to the warmer wall.

archive_06_015.speaker: narrator
archive_06_015.text: The day's final stock report showed twenty shares issued over the first two days and one sack of charcoal used in two measured halves. Ninety-five sacks and one thousand and forty kitchen shares remained. The cold forecast would change the following days' heat allowance. Tan checked the safe brazier and ventilation before authorising the first full-sack firing. The notice named actual use rather than pretending the planned seventy-two cold days had already occurred. Yue copied the figures onto the staff board, then went to mend the other cuff of her coat.

archive_06_016.speaker: narrator
archive_06_016.text: The weather turned on the thirty-ninth night. Wind struck the new slates with a dry tapping like fingernails on a table, and the hall windows held a pale fringe of frost by dawn. The carpenter's repair joints stayed dry. An old gutter beyond the repaired span filled with frozen leaves, spilling water onto the outside steps. The duty worker closed those steps until the blockage could be cleared safely. Luo moved the morning readers to the checked side door and placed a person there to direct them, not merely an arrow no one expected.

archive_06_017.speaker: narrator
archive_06_017.text: Sun arrived using that side door and accused the archive of moving itself while she was away. Luo offered to draw another blue sheep pointing at the entrance. She said she had come for the common school minute extract she had agreed to clarify, not for his menagerie. The agreed question concerned which meeting she attended and whether the minute book's attendance name represented her. She compared the date with her own old calendar note and confirmed it. She did not expand the statement into the founder's intentions when the clerk's pen paused expectantly.

archive_06_018.speaker: narrator
archive_06_018.text: Afterwards she stayed for tea at the open table, using the public room as a visitor rather than extending the appointment. Yue asked what she had been reading lately. Sun said a neighbour had lent her a travel account whose author described mountains entirely by the meals available beside them. She thought it an improvement on accounts which noticed only dangerous heights. Luo claimed the archive's kitchen deserved a chapter. The cook, passing through, said his chapter would begin by returning the borrowed strainer he had hidden behind a catalogue box.

archive_06_019.speaker: narrator
archive_06_019.text: The strainer had indeed become a support for loose catalogue slips. Luo returned it washed and offered to buy a replacement tray from his own purse. Dai told him the office already owned a slip tray if he could bear to find it. They searched the desk together and discovered it under a stack of superseded notices. Sun laughed until she needed to rest, then asked someone to fetch her walking stick. The request ended the amusement without making it a crisis. Yue brought the stick and waited for Sun to name the help she wanted.

archive_06_020.speaker: narrator
archive_06_020.text: Outside, Sun needed an elbow on the frosted threshold and a pause at the courtyard's sound handrail. She declined a cart ride home because its jolt hurt her hip. Her appointed neighbour accompanied her along the cleared village path. Yue watched them leave, aware that a safe exit involved more than opening a door. Tan had asked the carpenter to fit a lower rail at the side entrance for shorter visitors. The materials were ordinary and available from the roof project's accepted leftover timber, with the carpenter's new minor-work authorisation recorded separately.

archive_06_021.speaker: narrator
archive_06_021.text: The rail cost four copper in fitting labour from the qualified-work allowance. Its small timber piece was recorded as an authorised reuse of the accepted project leftover, reducing no beam that still carried the roof. The remaining allowance fell from one hundred and forty-five to one hundred and forty-one. Dai wanted the receipt attached to the accessibility inspection rather than lost among casual desk expenses. Yue helped the clerk do it. A practical change could be cheap and still deserve a traceable reason.

archive_06_022.speaker: narrator
archive_06_022.text: He came to report that his father had signed the limited path statement. He would attend the preliminary session if the road remained safe. He's mother had chosen to submit her own statement separately rather than sign a combined family account. The two narratives overlapped without matching in every detail. The father remembered buying a shovel before the drain work; the mother remembered borrowing one because the purchased shovel broke. The registrar could compare the specifics. He had not asked either parent to erase a memory simply to make the family look united.

archive_06_023.speaker: narrator
archive_06_023.text: The orchard representative arrived with a revised statement of trustee expenditure. She had removed one invoice previously described as house repair after the carpenter explained it served the public path drainage. That cost could not be presented as a private improvement to the disputed house. She still claimed genuine roof and wall expenses and lawful authority for the later letting based on the catalogue information they received. Dai's institutional apology did not absolve the trustees of checking an instrument, but it explained why their decision had not begun with a knowingly forged claim.

archive_06_024.speaker: narrator
archive_06_024.text: The representative brought a message from the present occupant's contact. He wished to remain in the house while the dispute was heard and would allow an ordinary condition survey under a specific appointment. He did not offer photographs of his private rooms for the public archive summary. The registrar would consider temporary occupation arrangements at the preliminary session. He Xi read the message without asking the representative why the occupant had not come personally. He had now seen his father's stiff hand struggle with a coat fastening and understood that travel could cost a body more than its fare.

archive_06_025.speaker: narrator
archive_06_025.text: At the archive, Dai received a letter from her daughter asking whether the repaired roof meant she could come down for winter. Yue did not read the private page. Dai mentioned the invitation herself while setting aside a public accession check. Her daughter lived in a warmer district and had room for her. She had been inviting Dai for years. This time she named a particular train of carts before the seasonal road closure, making the invitation more practical and therefore harder to dismiss as something she could consider whenever work finally ended.

archive_06_026.speaker: dai_shuren
archive_06_026.text: I have made my retirement sound like a reward the archive will give me after it becomes perfect. That is a very convenient way never to take it. My daughter has stopped asking whether the work is finished. She asks whether someone else can do it for a season. The answer ought to be yes. I have trained people to guard packets and use lists, but perhaps I have trained them less thoroughly to contradict me. If I leave one day, I would prefer the archive to remain capable of refusing my instructions.

archive_06_027.speaker: narrator
archive_06_027.text: She began a deputy plan with Luo, naming functions rather than granting him every authority she held. Restricted deposit decisions required their existing second approvals; procurement retained the board member's signature; treatment belonged to Tan; opening schedules belonged to the designated steward under the board rule. Luo objected that distributing her role would take longer than simply appointing him. Dai said that speed was exactly what had put a house instrument into a school wrapper. He winced and accepted the point, then asked her to avoid teaching it by mentioning that wrapper every morning.

archive_06_028.speaker: narrator
archive_06_028.text: The exchange grew warmer after they both laughed. Yue copied the function list and found fewer abbreviations than in the first-day notices. Dai asked her to read it as someone who might arrive after winter and know neither custodian's habits. Yue identified a review deadline missing from the temporary closure section. Luo added it without defending the old version. Tan wanted a named substitute if she herself became ill. The plan acquired two more spaces for ordinary board appointments. It was beginning to resemble an institution people could inhabit without becoming its permanent spine.

archive_06_029.speaker: narrator
archive_06_029.text: Dai later took her daughter's letter to her own room and began an answer. She wrote that the roof was repaired, then crossed out the next sentence about coming when everything settled. It had appeared in too many earlier letters. She offered a specific spring visit after the winter appointment review, subject to the road, and asked what dates suited the household receiving her. The page did not resign her post. It made the desire to leave for a season visible enough that someone else could answer it.

archive_06_030.speaker: narrator
archive_06_030.text: The fortieth day brought a thin fall of sleet. It melted on the courtyard stones but stayed on the higher ridge. The road watcher reported light carts still permitted under inspection, with closure possible if the temperature fell overnight. The preliminary session was four days away. Its notice already named a review time for weather decisions. He checked it rather than leaving early to avoid a problem no one had yet confirmed. His father stayed in the rented family rooms and helped repair a broken chair with his sound hand, accepting help for the brace he could not hold.

archive_06_031.speaker: narrator
archive_06_031.text: Yue practised in the designated small training space after her work period. The approved grounded control had a quarter-unit delivery ceiling and a separate recorded command cost, isolated from the archive's heating supply. She kept to the stage-five forms she had earned, repeating a release sequence whose final movement had become hurried under fatigue. The day's value lay in making the ending less abrupt, not in opening another pair. Outside the room, a dropped kitchen lid made her jump. She laughed at the disproportion, reset the ordinary bench arrangement and ended the session while her attention was still sound.

archive_06_032.speaker: narrator
archive_06_032.text: Tan found her washing the practice leads and asked whether winter rest felt different from road rest. Yue said the road had always offered the illusion that another place might make her less tired. Here she would have to notice tiredness without packing it onto a cart. Tan said the archive offered a similar illusion through unfinished stacks. A person could believe one more box would make rest possible until the next box arrived. They went to supper before either tested the theory. The cook's bell, unlike an unfinished box, supplied an actual ending.

archive_06_033.speaker: narrator
archive_06_033.text: The mild first two days had used one fuel sack. Two colder days then used one each, leaving ninety-three at the close of day forty. Forty daily shares had been issued since winter stores opened, leaving one thousand and twenty. No overnight guests had entered the winter sleeping roster yet. The common notice put these figures beside the forecast without converting them into a promised departure day. The board's assumptions still looked adequate. Dai nevertheless sent the first scheduled supply check to the lower receiving house, keeping the contact active while the route was open.

archive_06_034.speaker: narrator
archive_06_034.text: A reply from the regional preservation office offered a short visit before deep snow to complete assessment of several damp packets. Its qualified worker would require five days' fee and board at the agreed rate. Tan prioritised three items whose owners had accepted the treatment assessment. The archive would not summon expertise merely to display a new tool. Dai asked for an itemised offer against the remaining qualified allowance before approving. Winter operating money had finite tasks attached, and the recently fitted rail had a claim as real as an interesting damaged page.

archive_06_035.speaker: narrator
archive_06_035.text: The offer totalled thirty copper for the appointment and ordinary return transport, with visitor food drawn from the recorded kitchen shares. The board contact approved it, reducing the qualified allowance from one hundred and forty-one to one hundred and eleven. The worker would arrive on day forty-two if the road stayed open and remain through day forty-six. Five additional daily shares were therefore provisionally expected, but would be issued only for actual attendance. The receiving room's first temporary bed was reserved without adding a person to the permanent ten-resident baseline.

archive_06_036.speaker: narrator
archive_06_036.text: He heard the visiting worker might delay on the ridge and offered his courier route information. The information cost nothing to repeat, but if he accompanied the visitor it would require a paid appointment and could not be presumed within his family's petition duties. Dai thanked him for the route assessment and selected the ordinary carter already booked by the preservation office. He looked pleased not to have been asked to solve the journey himself. He had promised his mother a morning repairing their rented room's loose shutter before the session.

archive_06_037.speaker: narrator
archive_06_037.text: On the forty-first afternoon, the house occupant's contact asked the registrar to move the preliminary session closer to the house. The occupant had become unwell after a cold spell and could not travel. The registrar proposed allowing his appointed contact to attend while arranging his limited statement through the local authorised procedure. He Xi worried that the sickness would prevent any decision. The clerk explained that notice and representation could still support preliminary directions, while final disputed findings might need further participation. He was learning how a process could continue without pretending the missing person had ceased to matter.

archive_06_038.speaker: narrator
archive_06_038.text: The same letter asked the family not to enter the house or attempt repairs before temporary directions were made. He had not planned to, but his father had offered to mend its gate after seeing the old hinge fail. A well-meant repair might blur possession and expose them to an allegation that they had taken control. He told his father, who looked humiliated. His mother said there were enough broken things in their rented room to occupy willing hands. The father went back to the shutter. The offered help found somewhere it was wanted and permitted.

archive_06_039.speaker: narrator
archive_06_039.text: He and his father quarrelled over the rented shutter that evening. The father insisted his old repair method would hold; He pointed to the widened screw hole and reached for a different brace. Their voices rose until He's mother asked which of them intended to sleep in the draught. They stopped. The father accepted the new brace, and He held it where his father's injured hand could not. Afterwards neither apologised elegantly. They tested the closed shutter together and found the room quieter.

archive_06_040.speaker: narrator
archive_06_040.text: Yue encountered him there while returning a message through the village clerk's public route. He was balancing the shutter on a stool while his wife held it steady. He asked Yue whether the archive still needed workers who could not lift a full box. She said copying, inspection and receipt work mattered too, but appointments depended on actual vacancies and training. He nodded as if she had given him a useful answer rather than a promise. She saw how easily sympathy could have become an invented job, and was glad the existing work was broad enough to describe honestly.

archive_06_041.speaker: narrator
archive_06_041.text: The preservation worker arrived on the forty-second morning with a compact kit, her office appointment and the carter's route receipt. Tan met her at the side door and showed the approved three-item assessment list. The visitor inspected room conditions before opening any kit compartment. Her first recommendation was to move the table farther from the warming air stream, where a worker's comfort had created uneven drying conditions. Tan moved it without arguing. A hired specialist could improve the room precisely because the resident staff had not tried to make her visit ceremonial.

archive_06_042.speaker: narrator
archive_06_042.text: On Yue's rest day, the ordinary assistant prepared the condition sheets while the visitor assessed the first packet. The missing text at its damp edge remained missing. The assessment identified a safe support and future storage position, not a recovered sentence. Its owner would receive that practical improvement in a report. Luo looked disappointed and then helped carry the new support instead of asking for a more impressive result. The visitor said the absence of another lost edge next winter would not look dramatic in a before-and-after picture. It would nevertheless be the result worth paying her to achieve.

archive_06_043.speaker: narrator
archive_06_043.text: The worker's kitchen share was entered with the ten resident shares. At the end of day forty-two, sixty-one shares had been issued across six days, leaving nine hundred and ninety-nine. The first two mild days and following four cold days had used five sacks in total, leaving ninety-one. Tan kept the damp old sacks excluded. Their merchant had now agreed to collect them on a return route but had made no accepted replacement delivery. A promise below did not warm the hall above.

archive_06_044.speaker: narrator
archive_06_044.text: The sleet became snow during the forty-third night. By morning the courtyard wore a thin white cover, and the ridge had vanished into low cloud. The archive's winter hall kept its tables dry beneath the new timber. Staff entered through the cleared side approach, knocking snow from boots before reaching the floor mats. Yue stood at the window and watched the duty worker clear a narrow path to the store. For the first time the room matched the winter pictures she had imagined from the receiving-house notice, though reality included a broom and an impatient cook.

archive_06_045.speaker: narrator
archive_06_045.text: The road watcher closed carts pending inspection. The registrar invoked the session's published weather review rather than allowing claimants to assemble blindly below. The forty-fourth-day preliminary session would be postponed to the next safe date, and all parties received the same notice through the established message points. He read the archive's copy with his jaw tight. His mother had arranged paid leave, his father had promised to come, and witnesses had held their mornings available. An honest weather decision still imposed real costs. The registrar asked for those costs to be recorded for scheduling review.

archive_06_046.speaker: he_xi
archive_06_046.text: I am not angry that they refused to put a cart on a closed road. I am angry because I had finally made enough plans to imagine the morning happening. My mother has to ask for another day. The neighbour has to decide whether she can still wait before travelling. My father looks relieved, and I do not know whether that is his hand or his fear. I will not tell anyone the closure is a trick. I need an hour to dislike it without becoming unfair.

archive_06_047.speaker: narrator
archive_06_047.text: The archive gave him the hour without charging it to his courier task. He sat in the receiving room with his own bread and the family appointment papers. Yue continued preparing the movement record, which would remain useful on the next date. She neither interrupted his silence nor withdrew into cold professionalism. At the end of her copying period she asked whether he wanted to walk the cleared yard once. He did. Snow fell on the repaired roof quietly enough that they could hear water moving inside the new gutter.

archive_06_048.speaker: narrator
archive_06_048.text: The preservation visit could continue safely because the worker was already on the mountain. Her fifth day and return were now subject to the same road assessment as everyone else's. The appointment fee covered the agreed five days; any later work would need a new offer, while shelter during closure was handled under the receiving-room arrangements. Tan reserved enough assessed tasks for the remaining visit without assuming extra free labour. The visitor looked relieved at the distinction. She had spent too many past journeys proving herself helpful after weather had made her unable to leave.

archive_06_049.speaker: narrator
archive_06_049.text: Luo posted the changed public hours for the closed road period. Local mountain readers could still use safe sessions; distant visitors would not be urged upward. The urgent enquiry channel remained open through the lower message point when relays could travel safely. Dai reviewed the appointment and supply positions with the duty staff. The roof repair was holding. The winter stock still exceeded the programme's expected use. These facts made snow manageable, though they could not restore the preliminary session's lost morning. Yue listened to the report and then heard the cook ask who had left boots beside the stove.

archive_06_050.speaker: narrator
archive_06_050.text: The boots belonged to the preservation visitor, whose soaked soles needed ordinary drying away from excessive heat. The cook moved them to the proper rack and returned the visitor's embarrassed apology with a lecture she gave resident staff equally. At supper the visitor imitated the lecture with enough affection to make the cook laugh. Dai looked surprised to find a temporary worker already contributing to the kitchen's jokes. Warmth entered the institution by such small permissions as well as through a carefully counted charcoal sack.

archive_06_051.speaker: narrator
archive_06_051.text: That night, the visitor told Tan she had nearly refused the mountain appointment. Her daughter hated her travelling in cold weather, and she hated returning home too proud of useful work to admit how tired it made her. Tan said she had imagined regional specialists arrived without such doubts. The visitor laughed and showed the blister at the heel of her thick boot. Yue, listening from the next chair with their invitation, felt the room grow easier to inhabit. Expertise could sit beside a blister without losing its authority.

archive_06_052.speaker: narrator
archive_06_052.text: Sun sent word that she would not come to the archive in snow for the specific school question. Her earlier signed clarification was complete, and any new question should reach her home through the agreed contact. Luo read the message without complaining that winter reduced available witnesses. It reduced available walkers. He sent a reply acknowledging the completed statement and asking whether she needed the borrowed jar brought back now or in spring. She replied that a clean jar could wait more patiently than a living person.

archive_06_053.speaker: narrator
archive_06_053.text: On the forty-fourth day, the registrar offered written preliminary directions that could be served without the postponed gathering, provided both sides had a chance to respond through their contacts. The directions would preserve current occupation, prevent unagreed changes to the disputed property and set deadlines for specific additional evidence. They would not declare final title or erase the recovered clause. He and the representative each requested a day to consult before replying. The office accepted the interval. A process slowed by snow could still do bounded useful work.

archive_06_054.speaker: narrator
archive_06_054.text: He's mother asked the archive clerk to help her understand the response deadline's date. The clerk read the calendar provision and showed where weather delays could be reported. He did not advise her which legal argument to choose. She brought the question to her appointed district adviser through the lower channel. He waited outside while she consulted the permitted procedure. The family claim was becoming less exclusively his own performance. He could be useful without speaking every sentence for the mother who had carried him to the archive fourteen years earlier.

archive_06_055.speaker: narrator
archive_06_055.text: The orchard representative agreed to preserve the property pending final resolution but wanted ordinary emergency repairs allowed with notice. The house occupant's contact supported that, since a broken flue should not wait on a title hearing. The registrar revised the proposed direction to distinguish preservation from improvements or changes in possession. He Xi accepted the practical exception with receipts and notice required. His father looked at the gate hinge and said it could wait; the occupant's heating could not. It was the first time the father had contributed without trying to repair something himself.

archive_06_056.speaker: narrator
archive_06_056.text: Yue helped Dai prepare the archive's response about its own errors. It accepted the catalogue and follow-up findings, waived the failed retrieval charge and offered the relevant certified extracts without making the family pay again for the institution's broken chain. Broader remedies would belong to the proper process. Dai would not purchase silence with a private apology, and Luo would not turn the apology into a public story carrying unapproved family details. Their joint letter stated the specific failures. Yue saw it signed by two people whose favourite explanations no longer fitted comfortably together.

archive_06_057.speaker: narrator
archive_06_057.text: The preservation worker completed the third assessment on day forty-six. Her five daily kitchen shares had been issued across her visit, and her promised work was finished. The road remained closed to her return cart that afternoon. The archive housed her in the same temporary bed while the next safe departure was assessed. She accepted no new treatment assignment that night. Tan invited her to sit by the open hall table with a borrowed public travel book. The woman chose the account which described mountains by their meals and laughed at its opinion of boiled turnips.

archive_06_058.speaker: narrator
archive_06_058.text: The cook added her ordinary cooking wood to the common store notice after the first snow. The annual kitchen allocation had stocked one hundred and twenty dry bundles before the winter programme, each tested for a normal day's cooking for the resident pot. Ten had now been used, leaving one hundred and ten, apart from the hall's charcoal. Kindling came within those bundles. A larger guest pot might use more, and she would enter the actual bundle issue. The cupboard of food did not heat itself.

archive_06_059.speaker: narrator
archive_06_059.text: At the close of day forty-six, the ten residents had used one hundred shares across ten days and the visitor five, leaving nine hundred and fifty-five. The heat use was one sack for the first two mild days plus eight sacks for the eight colder days, leaving eighty-seven. The duty sheet showed both calculations plainly. It did not subtract an imagined rest-day meal or add a damp sack because a merchant had promised collection. The cook placed the remaining food total beside her next day's pots, then closed the store door.

archive_06_060.speaker: narrator
archive_06_060.text: He read the common stock notice while waiting for his paid route assignment to reopen. He said the kitchen shares looked easier than an inheritance clause because at least a bowl was a bowl. The cook heard him and pointed out that a child's bowl, a labourer's bowl and a sick person's bowl could contain different things. Her daily share was a planning unit, not a command to make every stomach identical. He bowed extravagantly and withdrew his claim. Yue laughed, delighted that he could now receive correction without hearing every correction as rejection.

archive_06_061.speaker: narrator
archive_06_061.text: The registrar's revised temporary directions were accepted through the parties' contacts. The current occupant would remain while title and remedies were investigated. The trustees would maintain necessary safety work under notice and receipt. The family would not enter or change possession unilaterally. Both sides would preserve the records already identified. The recovered descendant instrument remained part of the legal comparison, and final resolution would wait for the competent hearing. He found the arrangement frustrating but read it to his father and mother without changing its words into either victory or defeat.

archive_06_062.speaker: narrator
archive_06_062.text: That evening his father returned to the rented rooms alone while He stayed for a short conversation with Yue in the open public hour. He said the temporary direction had made a strange kind of room for him: he could go on working without being accused of abandoning the house claim. His mother could finish her winter kitchen shifts. His father could decide whether to stay locally or return to his own work when the road opened. None of those ordinary decisions erased the disputed right. He had begun to need that distinction as much as any document.

archive_06_063.speaker: narrator
archive_06_063.text: Yue watched snow gather beyond the winter hall's window while the public readers turned their sheets. The room no longer looked like a repaired autumn interior hoping to pass an inspection. It looked inhabited by a season that would test its plans. Dai checked the closed deposit screen, Luo guided a local reader to the proper public copy and Tan let the finished visiting specialist read without asking her to keep treating pages. At the table beside Yue, He folded the temporary direction carefully. Ordinary rain had become snow; ordinary work had become winter.
